name: subagent-for-large-context
query: I need to understand how authentication flows across about 80 files in a legacy Java monolith so I can plan a refactor. I do not want this exploration to fill up my main conversation with code snippets I will not touch.
expected_behavior: Restate the scenario in one sentence.
Answer the DIAGNOSTICO.md question set, flagging context size as large and objective as investigation.
Recommend a subagent as the primary primitive, citing docs/claude/agentes/02-subagentes.md.
Explain that the subagent returns a summary and the main session receives only the summary, cited to docs/claude/harness/06-janela-de-contexto.md.
Recommend a skill only if the investigation pattern will repeat; otherwise state that no skill is needed and justify.
State at least one rejected alternative (for example reading files in the main session) with the reason it fails the context-preservation requirement.
Specify guardrails: read-only tool set for the subagent, no edits.
Propose adoption metric: main-session token growth before and after adopting the pattern.
forbidden_behavior: Recommend creating a permanent skill without evidence the investigation will repeat.
Recommend a routine (the scenario is a one-off).
Recommend giving the subagent edit tools.
Skip citing docs/claude/harness/06-janela-de-contexto.md when justifying the context isolation benefit.
Recommend agent teams for a single investigation.
success_criteria: Subagent is the primary primitive with correct doc citation.
Tool set is scoped to read/search only.
The recommendation is honest about the trade-off (extra model call, summary may drop nuance) per TRADE-OFFS.md.
No permanent artifact (skill, plugin) is proposed unless justified.
